widgets_values:
subject_definitions:
<Video 1> is the source footage for this video: one continuous vertical medium shot from the thighs up, filmed indoors in front of a dark teal door and a light beige marble wall, soft warm indoor lighting, a static camera with slight handheld movement. One young woman dances playfully to music facing the camera: she poses with one hand raised beside her face, sways her shoulders and hips, brings her fingers to her lips, turns her head quickly so her hair swings, then spreads both arms out to the sides with open palms and waves her hands while swaying. In the source footage, the dancing woman's head, face, hair and clothing are marked as reconstruction zones; these positions in the final video are replaced with the face, hair and outfit of <Subject 1>. Scene, lighting, light position and brightness strictly follow the corresponding moments in <Video 1>. Movements, camera framing and editing rhythm strictly follow <Video 1>. Only the single dancing woman is replaced; the dark teal door, the beige marble wall and the room remain fully preserved.
<Subject 1> stands for the adult woman shown in <Picture 1> (full outfit) and <Picture 2> (face close-up), who replaces the dancing woman. Her face identity comes only from <Picture 2>, and only body motion, hand gestures, head turns, gaze and expression come from <Video 1>: woman in her mid-twenties, oval face with soft East Asian features, fair skin, defined eyeliner and glossy red lips, black hair gathered at the crown into one high ponytail with one long braid falling behind the right shoulder and thin loose strands framing the forehead, silver hoop earrings, glossy black latex long-sleeved bodysuit with a high collar, front zipper, chest cutout and side waist cutouts, black latex shorts, glossy black lace-up thigh-high platform boots; all dancing, swaying, hand gestures and head turns follow the corresponding motion in <Video 1>.

summary:
The target video is an edited version of <Video 1>. The dancing woman becomes <Subject 1> while the dance moves, hand gestures, camera framing, the teal door and the marble wall are retained. Every action shown on screen already exists within <Video 1>.

retention_analysis:
<Video 1> (editing source, motion and editing structure): partially_preserved - the teal door, the marble wall, the room, lighting, motion timing and camera framing stay fully preserved; the dancing woman's head and clothing are processed as reconstruction zones, and these positions in the final video are replaced with the face, hair and outfit of <Subject 1>.
<Subject 1> ([Shot 1]): fully_preserved - face, skin tone, red lips, high ponytail with one long braid, silver hoop earrings, glossy black latex bodysuit with cutouts and black latex shorts.

detailed_description:
Vertical 9:16 live-action indoor footage with soft warm lighting; light position and background strictly follow <Video 1>.
[Shot 1] <Subject 1> stands facing the camera in front of the teal door, raises one hand beside her face with a playful smile, sways her shoulders and hips, touches her fingertips to her lips, turns her head quickly so her braided ponytail swings, then spreads both arms out to the sides with open palms and waves her hands while swaying to the music.

nodes.title: How to use
widgets_values:
Character Swap (MiniMax H3)

1. Reference Video: load the source clip. frame_load_cap = length (124 = 5 s, 175 = 7.3 s; 17k+5 frames at 24 fps).
2. Reference Image1: full-body image of the new character. Its face is cropped automatically (Auto Face Crop) and used as Picture 2.
3. SAM3 Mask: 'Mask target' = head (not person).
4. Write the Prompt (see 'How to write the swap prompt').
5. Stage 2 ON  -> Resolution Selector megapixels 0.5 (output x2, e.g. 1088x1920).
   Stage 2 OFF -> megapixels 1.0 (output e.g. 768x1376).
Tested best: Stage 2 ON. Singularity v2 + fl2v 8-step LoRA was best on the football clip.

nodes.title: How to write the swap prompt
widgets_values:
How to write the swap prompt (English only)

Sections: subject_definitions / summary / retention_analysis / detailed_description
Tags: <Video 1> source video, <Picture 1> full-body image, <Picture 2> face crop, <Subject 1> new character, [Shot 1]

RULES
1. Never name the original person's clothes, hat, glasses or jewellery. Write only:
   "the [role]'s head, face, hair and clothing are marked as reconstruction zones".
   Named items come back (a "cap" in the prompt made the cap reappear).
2. Call the original person by role only: "the seated guitarist", "the robed man".
3. Split identity: "Her face identity comes only from <Picture 2>, and only pose, gaze and
   expression come from <Video 1>".
4. Describe the new character in detail: age, face, skin, makeup, exact hairstyle,
   accessories, every clothing item with colour/material, shoes.
5. List everything that must stay: other people, props, background
   ("...the goalkeeper, the white football and the advertising boards remain fully preserved").
6. Lock motion: "Movements, camera framing and editing rhythm strictly follow <Video 1>"
   and "Every action shown on screen already exists within <Video 1>."
7. detailed_description: tell the events in the same order as the video.

TEMPLATE (subject_definitions)
<Video 1> is the source footage for this video: [shot type]. [what happens]. In the source
footage, the [role]'s head, face, hair and clothing are marked as reconstruction zones; these
positions in the final video are replaced with the face, hair and outfit of <Subject 1>.
Scene, lighting, light position and brightness strictly follow the corresponding moments in
<Video 1>. Movements, camera framing and editing rhythm strictly follow <Video 1>. Only the
single [role] is replaced; [everything else] remain fully preserved.
<Subject 1> stands for the [woman/man] shown in <Picture 1> (full outfit) and <Picture 2>
(face close-up), who replaces the [role]. Her face identity comes only from <Picture 2>, and
only [motion] come from <Video 1>: [new character details].

Full template + an AI prompt that writes it for you: prompts/h3-character-swap-prompt-writer.md

nodes.title: Resize source video to generation size (saves RAM)
Encode stage-2 references first (keeps VRAM free)
Note: RDNA4 settings
widgets_values:
## RDNA4 settings (R9700, 32 GB VRAM, 64 GB RAM)

Changes from the 5090 workflow:
- **Default output 720p**: Resolution megapixels **0.225** -> stage 1 352x640 -> stage 2 704x1280.
  For 960x1728 set 0.4, for 1088x1920 set 0.5 (slower, more RAM; see the table).
- **Reference Video loads 124 frames (5 s)** by default. frame_load_cap 0 loads the whole clip, which on this card
  means a much longer run and more RAM. Keep lengths at 17k+5 frames (124, 175, 226).
- **One VAE**: Load VAE (BF16) with the int8 ConvRot video VAE does all encodes and the decode, through
  **VAE Chunked Conv3D** (ComfyUI-RDNA4-Accel). Without it the reference-video encode asks for one 7 GB conv buffer
  and runs out of VRAM when the model from the previous run is still loaded. The fp16 VAE loader is muted (5 GB less RAM).
- **Encode stage-2 references first** (VRAM_Debug): both reference encodes run before the DiT is loaded.
- **Text Encoder BF16** after Load CLIP.
- **Sparse attention** on stage 1 too (tau 1.5 from 25 % of the steps); stage 2 tau 1.3 -> 1.5.
- **Mem Eff Sage Attention Patch** is bypassed: it needs CUDA sageattention and fails on ROCm.
  Low VRAM Attention and Chunk FeedForward (KJ) stay on: same output, less peak VRAM.
- **Stage 1 video** is not decoded unless you need it: the stage-2 size now comes from the resized source frames.
  When you switch Stage 2 off, switch **Stage 1 video (on/off)** on to get the stage-1 result.
- Model files: Singularity ref2va **v1.3** pruned int8, ref2v turbo 4-step v1.0 768p, 3D latent upscaler bf16,
  2K refiner **r128** (the rank-16 file is not published; DrakenZA's swiglu-fixed r128 is used).

Measured on the R9700 (220 W), 5 s source clip (124 frames), Singularity v1.3, run right after the previous one:

| Output | Stage 1 | Stage 2 | Total | RAM peak |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **704x1280 (0.225)** | 10 x 11.7 s | 3 x 29.2 s | **463 s** (cold models) | **50 GB** |
| 960x1728 (0.4) | 10 x 27.2 s | 3 x 76.5 s | 773 s | 56 GB |
| 960x1728, before tuning | 10 x 40 s | out of VRAM | - | 61 GB + swap |

Outfit, motion and background follow the references and the source at both sizes; 720p is a little softer.
RAM above ~58 GB means swapping: then restart ComfyUI before the next run.

nodes.title: Note: Identity settings
widgets_values:
## Identity settings (closer to the reference character)

Measured on the same clip and seed (face similarity to the reference image, OpenCV SFace; 0.363 = same person):

| Setting | Face similarity (mean) | Same-person frames |
|---|---|---|
| Before: mask head, refs 'match', 2K refiner LoRA 1.0, sigmas 0.909 | 0.24 | 1 / 16 |
| Mask person + refs fixed size | 0.26 | 3 / 16 |
| + refiner LoRA 0.4 | 0.26 | 5 / 16 |
| **+ no refiner LoRA, sigmas 0.7 (now)** | **0.35** | **8 / 16** |

What changed:
- **SAM3 mask target = person**: the whole source person is grey in the reference video, so the source body and outfit do not leak. Motion still follows the source (the mask follows the body). Use **head** only when you want to keep the source outfit.
- **References at a fixed size**: Reference Image1 is scaled to 0.5 MP and the face crop is 768x768, with ref_image_size **max** on both Reference to Video nodes. 'match' shrank them to the stage-1 size (a 470 px face at 720p).
- **Stage 2 keeps the character**: the 2K regenerate LoRA is bypassed and stage 2 uses the gentle sigmas (0.7). The refiner at 0.909 re-drew the person: tanned skin, muscular legs, a sharper face. Stage 2 is also faster (2 steps).

- **Grow mask 3 px** (was 12): with the person mask, a grown silhouette is wider than the real body and the model fills all of it, so the character came out bulky (wide shoulders, thick arms). 3 px keeps the source proportions. Face similarity on this seed: 0.26 (12 px: 0.35); both pass on some frames, faces are small at 720p.

Tips: a reference image with the same framing as the video (full body for a full-body dance) works best; body proportions still follow the source dancer's pose.
